newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNIP sees 79,000 ha rise in French field pea area.
newsitem.headline: UNIP sees 79,000 ha rise in French field pea area.

text.p: French farmers are expected to sow more field peas for animal feed proteins in 1997 than in the previous year, industry group UNIP said on Friday.

A joint survey conducted in April by UNIP and French crop quality institute ITCF suggests 1997 field pea sowings may rise by 79,000 hectares over 1996 to around 615,000 ha, UNIP said in a routine report. This would represent a rise of more than 14 percent over 1996.
The prediction exceeds an estimate released by the farm ministry earlier this week of a 10 percent rise in protein pea sowings to 582,000 hectares from 531,000 hectares.
UNIP said area sown to field peas in 1997 would however remain below the 661,500 ha sown in 1994 and the 737,500 ha sown in 1993.
Among key production regions, the Picardy area should experience the sharpest increase in area following last year's "excellent" yields, it said.
Area is also expected to rise in the Champagne region in the east, in central France, in Nord Pas de Calais, Britanny, and on irrigated patches of the Midi-Pyrenees and of the southeast.
Growth conditions for spring peas have improved following recent rainfalls and plant development is slightly ahead of an average year.

Cumulated rainfall since end April reached betwen 40 and 80 mm depending on region, partly or entirely replenishing ground water reserves for spring peas. This should be help sustain the crop until it reaches its crucial blooming stage. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
